trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Barcelona
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Sercotel Porta Barcelona
hotel.location: Generalitat de Catalunya, 6, Sant Just Desvern, ES (41.3772,2.0791)

experiences.name: Sagrada Família Guided Tour
experiences.description: Explore Gaudí's iconic basilica with a skip-the-line guided tour, including tower access for panoramic views of the Eixample district. Book a morning slot for the best light through the stained glass windows.

experiences.description: Self-guided or small-group walking tour through the Barri Gòtic, discovering Roman ruins, medieval palaces, and hidden plazas. Stay centrally located in El Born or Gothic Quarter hotels to walk directly to the starting point.

day_by_day.evening: Arrive at El Prat Airport at 19:20. Take the L9 Sud metro line to Torrassa, then transfer to L1 toward Sant Just Desvern area, or take a budget bus (Aerobús ~€6.75) to Plaça Catalunya and connect onward. Check in to Sercotel Porta Barcelona. Once settled, take a short evening stroll around Sant Just Desvern to get your bearings and grab a light dinner nearby.

meals.lunch: N/A - on the plane or airport
meals.dinner: Bar-restaurant near the hotel in Sant Just Desvern — look for a local 'menú del día' or a neighbourhood bocadillo bar. Budget ~€8–12 for a simple meal and drink.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — you'll be tired from travel. Pick up a T-Casual 10-trip metro card (~€11.35) at the airport metro station to save money on transport all week. The weather in August averages 28.9°C so pack light clothes and stay hydrated.

day_by_day.morning: Sagrada Família Guided Tour: Head into central Barcelona via metro (L3 or L5 to Sagrada Família stop). Arrive early (~9:00–9:30 AM) to beat the heat and crowds. Enjoy the skip-the-line guided tour with tower access for panoramic views of the city. Budget ~€26–36 for entry + towers. Spend 2–2.5 hours exploring Gaudí's iconic basilica inside and out.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Sagrada Família, walk or take a short metro ride to the Eixample district. Explore the Modernista architecture on the 'Block of Discord' (Manzana de la Discordia) on Passeig de Gràcia — admire Casa Batlló, Casa Amatller, and Casa Lleó Morera from the outside for free. Then stroll up to see the exterior of Casa Milà (La Pedrera). Window-shop and people-watch along Passeig de Gràcia.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the Gothic Quarter (Barri Gòtic) for the evening atmosphere. Wander the narrow medieval streets, grab a drink at a terrace bar, and soak in the nightlife buzz. Barcelona's nightlife starts late — bars fill up around 10–11 PM. Try a craft beer or local vermut at a Gothic Quarter bar.

meals.breakfast: Grab a coffee and croissant or tostada con tomate at a local café near the hotel or near Sagrada Família. Budget ~€3–5.
meals.lunch: Menú del día near Eixample — a 3-course lunch with bread and drink for ~€11–14. Look for side streets off Passeig de Gràcia for better value.
meals.dinner: Tapas at a budget bar in the Gothic Quarter — patatas bravas, pan con tomate, croquetas. Budget ~€12–16 per person including a drink.

day_by_day.notes: Book Sagrada Família tickets online in advance to guarantee skip-the-line access and avoid sellouts. August is peak season. Wear comfortable walking shoes — you'll cover 6–8 km today.

day_by_day.morning: Gothic Quarter Architecture Walk: Start early (~9:00 AM) before the heat peaks. Follow a self-guided walking tour through the Barri Gòtic — discover the Roman walls and Temple d'August (free entry to the courtyard), the Barcelona Cathedral (free entry before 12:30 PM), Plaça de Sant Jaume, and the medieval Pont del Bisbe. Pick up a free map from the tourist office or use a free app like Google Maps with offline Gothic Quarter highlights.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk from the Gothic Quarter down to the waterfront via La Rambla (stay alert for pickpockets). Explore the free Barceloneta beach — take a swim and relax on the sand. Then walk along the Port Olímpic promenade and admire Frank Gehry's golden 'Peix' (Fish) sculpture. Cool off with a granizado (iced drink) from a beach kiosk (~€3–4).
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Gothic Quarter or El Born neighbourhood for Barcelona's famous nightlife. Start with pre-drinks ('botellón' style or a cheap bar) around 10 PM, then explore the bar scene in El Born — Carrer del Parlament and Carrer del Rec are great streets. Many bars have no cover charge until midnight.

meals.breakfast: Granja-style café in the Gothic Quarter — churros with chocolate or a café amb llet and toast. Budget ~€4–6.
meals.lunch: Mercat de la Boqueria or Mercat de Santa Caterina (less touristy, cheaper) — grab fresh fruit, a bocadillo, or a market stall meal. Budget ~€6–10.
meals.dinner: El Born neighbourhood pintxos bar — many bars offer pintxos (small bites on bread) for €1.50–2.50 each. Order 4–6 and a drink for ~€12–15.

day_by_day.notes: The Gothic Quarter walk is entirely free and one of the best architecture experiences in Barcelona. Start before 10 AM to avoid the worst heat and tourist crowds. Apply sunscreen — 28.9°C average high means it will be hot by midday.

day_by_day.morning: Take the metro to Lesseps or Vallcarca and hike up to Parc Güell (free to enter the monumental zone requires a ticket ~€10, but the surrounding park and viewpoints are free). Arrive by 9:00 AM to enjoy the panoramic views of Barcelona before the crowds and heat arrive. Explore Gaudí's mosaic terraces, the viaducts, and the free wooded paths. The views of the city skyline and sea are spectacular.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head back down to Gràcia neighbourhood — one of Barcelona's most charming and local districts. Wander the Plaça del Sol and Plaça de la Vila de Gràcia, browse independent boutiques and vintage shops, and explore the colourful streets. Visit the free exterior of Casa Vicens (Gaudí's first major work) — entry is ~€16 but the exterior is impressive and free to admire.
day_by_day.evening: Gràcia has a fantastic local nightlife scene that's less touristy and more affordable than the Gothic Quarter. Head to Plaça del Sol or Plaça de la Virreina around 9–10 PM where locals gather for outdoor drinks. Then explore the bars on Carrer de Verdi or Carrer de Torrijos for live music and a relaxed vibe.

meals.breakfast: Pick up pastries and coffee from a local bakery (forn de pa) near the hotel or in Gràcia. Budget ~€3–5.
meals.lunch: Menú del día in Gràcia neighbourhood — excellent value local restaurants offer 3 courses + drink for ~€11–13. Try streets around Plaça de la Virreina.
meals.dinner: Budget restaurant in Gràcia — try a local Catalan restaurant with a set dinner menu or a falafel/kebab spot for ~€8–12.

day_by_day.notes: The monumental zone of Parc Güell requires timed tickets — book online in advance (~€10). The rest of the park is free. Bring water and a hat for the uphill walk in August heat. Gràcia is very walkable and has a great neighbourhood feel.

day_by_day.morning: Take the metro to Paral·lel and ride the free funicular up to Montjuïc. Explore the Jardins de Laribal and Jardí Botànic (free or ~€3.50) with stunning city views. Walk up to the Castell de Montjuïc (€5 entry) for panoramic views over the port and city. The architecture of the 1929 International Exposition pavilions — including the free exterior of the Mies van der Rohe Pavilion — is a must-see for architecture lovers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head back down to the city and visit the free Barceloneta neighbourhood one last time for a final swim or walk along the beach promenade. Browse the shops in El Raval or pick up budget souvenirs at the Mercat de Sant Antoni (open market on Sundays/weekdays). Pack your bags back at the hotel and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Final dinner in Barcelona — treat yourself to a slightly nicer meal within budget. Head to El Raval or Poble Sec for excellent value restaurants. Poble Sec's Carrer de Blai is famous for its pintxos bars — a fantastic and affordable final evening. Enjoy a last vermut or craft beer on a terrace before heading back to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast if included, or a café con leche and tostada con tomate at a local bar. Budget ~€3–5.
meals.lunch: Light lunch — bocadillo and fresh juice from a market or café. Budget ~€5–8. Keep it light before the journey home.
meals.dinner: Carrer de Blai pintxos crawl in Poble Sec — multiple bars with pintxos from €1–2.50 each. Budget ~€12–18 for a satisfying final meal with drinks.

day_by_day.notes: Check your return flight details and allow extra time for the journey back to the airport from Sant Just Desvern. The L9 Sud metro from Torrassa to the airport takes ~30–35 minutes. Budget tip: the T-Casual 10-trip card purchased on Day 1 should cover most of your metro journeys across the 5 days. Total estimated daily spend (excluding accommodation): €35–55 per day covering transport, entry fees, and meals.

day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Barcelona El Prat Airport at 19:20. Take the Aerobus or taxi (~25 min) to Sercotel Porta Barcelona in Sant Just Desvern. Check in, freshen up, and take a relaxed evening stroll around the local neighborhood to get oriented.

meals.lunch: N/A – on travel day or airport meal
meals.dinner: La Bodegueta del Penedès (Sant Just Desvern) – a cozy local wine bar and tapas spot near the hotel. Try the local cured meats and Catalan cheeses with a glass of Penedès wine. Budget ~€20–25 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light. Confirm hotel check-in details in advance as arrival is after 19:00. Exchange currency or use ATM at the airport. Pick up a T-Casual metro card (10-trip) for the week – it works on metro, bus, and FGC trains connecting Sant Just Desvern to central Barcelona.

day_by_day.morning: Sagrada Família Guided Tour – Take the FGC train from Sant Just Desvern to central Barcelona, then metro Line 2/5 to Sagrada Família. Arrive early (9:00–9:30) for your skip-the-line guided tour of Gaudí's iconic basilica, including tower access for panoramic views over the city. Allow 2–2.5 hours. Book tickets in advance online (~€35–40 per person with tower access).
day_by_day.afternoon: Gothic Quarter Architecture Walk – After lunch, head to the Barri Gòtic for a self-guided or small-group walking tour. Discover Roman ruins beneath the city, the Barcelona Cathedral, Plaça Reial, and medieval palaces. Pick up a free map from the tourist office or use a guided audio app. Wander through narrow lanes and pop into hidden courtyards. Allow 2–3 hours.
day_by_day.evening: Explore El Born neighborhood adjacent to the Gothic Quarter. Browse boutique shops and enjoy the vibrant atmosphere as the city cools down. End the evening with a leisurely walk along La Barceloneta beachfront promenade to soak in the summer sunset.

meals.breakfast: Café at the hotel or grab a croissant and café amb llet at a local bakery near Sant Just Desvern FGC station (~€4–6).
meals.lunch: Bar del Pla (El Born) – beloved local spot for Catalan cuisine. Try the croquetes de bacallà and a glass of house wine. Budget ~€18–22 per person.
meals.dinner: La Mar Salada (Barceloneta) – mid-range seafood restaurant near the beach. Excellent paella and fresh fish. Budget ~€30–35 per person.

day_by_day.notes: August heat peaks in the afternoon (up to 29°C). Wear light clothing, sunscreen, and carry a water bottle. The Sagrada Família is extremely popular – pre-booked timed entry is essential. Gothic Quarter streets are narrow and shaded, making it a good afternoon option.

day_by_day.morning: Palau de la Música Catalana Guided Morning Tour – Head to Sant Pere neighborhood for a guided tour of this breathtaking UNESCO-listed Modernista concert hall designed by Lluís Domènech i Montaner. Morning tours (10:00–11:00) showcase the stunning stained-glass skylight and ornate façade in beautiful natural light. Tickets ~€22 per person. Afterward, explore the surrounding Sant Pere neighborhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Tapas Crawl on Carrer del Parlament (Sant Antoni) – Take the metro to Sant Antoni and spend the afternoon grazing through the neighborhood's best tapas bars. Start around 14:00 when locals lunch. Sample patatas bravas, jamón ibérico, pan con tomate, and fresh anchovies across 3–4 bars. The Mercat de Sant Antoni nearby is also worth a browse for local produce and vintage books.
day_by_day.evening: Razzmatazz Club Night – Barcelona's legendary nightclub with five rooms spanning electronic, indie, and pop music. Doors open around 23:30–00:00; the club peaks between 01:00–04:00. Pre-purchase tickets online (~€15–20). Take a taxi or Uber from the hotel for safety late at night.

meals.breakfast: Federal Café (Sant Antoni area) – popular brunch spot with excellent coffee and avocado toast. Budget ~€10–14 per person.
meals.lunch: Tapas crawl on Carrer del Parlament – budget €25–30 per person across multiple bars including drinks.
meals.dinner: Bar Calders (Sant Antoni) – classic vermouth bar with excellent pintxos and small plates. Light pre-club dinner. Budget ~€15–20 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Razzmatazz is located in Poblenou (Carrer dels Almogàvers). Plan for a late night – consider a short nap in the early evening before heading out. Keep valuables secure in the club. Uber or licensed taxi recommended for the return journey to Sant Just Desvern late at night.

day_by_day.morning: Late, relaxed start after the club night. Head to Gràcia neighborhood – a charming bohemian village-within-the-city. Visit Casa Vicens (Gaudí's first major work, often overlooked by tourists, ~€16) and stroll through Plaça del Sol and Plaça de la Vila de Gràcia. Browse independent boutiques and street art.
day_by_day.afternoon: Park Güell – Walk or take a short taxi up to Gaudí's mosaic-tiled park for stunning views over Barcelona. Book the Monumental Zone timed entry in advance (~€10). Spend 1.5–2 hours exploring the dragon staircase, hypostyle room, and panoramic terrace. The surrounding free park areas are also beautiful for a stroll.
day_by_day.evening: Montjuïc at sunset – Take the cable car (Telefèric de Montjuïc, ~€12.70 return) up to the castle for sweeping views of the city and port glowing in the evening light. Afterward, head to Poble Sec for dinner and a nightcap in one of the lively bars on Carrer de Blai (pintxos street).

meals.breakfast: Late breakfast at La Pepita (Gràcia) – famous for creative montaditos and fresh juices. Budget ~€10–14 per person.
meals.lunch: Cervecería Catalana (Eixample) – iconic spot for tapas and cold beer. Try the mixed tapas platter. Budget ~€20–25 per person.
meals.dinner: Bodega Sepúlveda (Poble Sec) – rustic wine bar with excellent Catalan dishes and affordable wine list. Budget ~€22–28 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Park Güell timed entry sells out weeks in advance in August – book online before the trip. The cable car to Montjuïc may have queues; alternatively, Bus 150 runs to the castle. Carrer de Blai in Poble Sec is lively from 20:00 onward and great for a casual evening without a big spend.

day_by_day.morning: Eixample Modernisme Walk – Spend the morning exploring the elegant Eixample grid, Barcelona's showcase of Modernista architecture. Walk the 'Block of Discord' (Manzana de la Discordia) on Passeig de Gràcia: admire Casa Batlló (exterior or interior tour ~€35 if desired), Casa Amatller, and Casa Lleó Morera. Window-shop the luxury boutiques and photograph the iconic hexagonal pavement tiles.
day_by_day.afternoon: Barceloneta Beach & Port Olímpic – Spend the hottest part of the day at the beach. Rent a sun lounger (~€6–8), swim in the Mediterranean, and enjoy the relaxed coastal atmosphere. Afterward, stroll through Port Olímpic marina and browse the waterfront. Consider a short boat trip (Las Golondrinas, ~€15) for a different perspective of the city skyline.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner in El Born followed by a final evening walk through the illuminated Gothic Quarter. Raise a glass of cava at a rooftop bar – try the Terraza del Hotel Arts or a more budget-friendly option like La Isabela Rooftop (Hotel 1898, Ramblas) for panoramic night views of Barcelona.

meals.breakfast: Forn de Sant Jaume (Passeig de Gràcia area) – traditional Catalan bakery with excellent ensaïmades and coffee. Budget ~€6–9 per person.
meals.lunch: La Cova Fumada (Barceloneta) – legendary no-frills local bar, birthplace of the bombas (meat croquette). Cash only, arrive early as it closes when food runs out. Budget ~€15–18 per person.
meals.dinner: El Xampanyet (El Born) – iconic cava bar and tapas restaurant with house cava and classic Catalan bites. Perfect farewell dinner. Budget ~€25–30 per person.

day_by_day.notes: If departing the next day, pack bags the night before and confirm transport to the airport. El Xampanyet is very popular – arrive at opening time (19:00) to avoid a long wait. August evenings stay warm and lively well past midnight, so enjoy the final night at a relaxed pace.

trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Barcelona El Prat Airport at 19:20 on TAP Air Portugal. A pre-arranged private luxury transfer (Mercedes E-Class or similar) whisks you to Sercotel Porta Barcelona in Sant Just Desvern (~20 min). Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely stroll around the quiet residential neighbourhood to decompress from travel.

meals.dinner: Dinner at El Celler de Can Roca's sister concept or locally, visit Restaurante Àbac (2 Michelin stars, ~25 min drive into Barcelona) for a late tasting menu starting around 21:00 – perfectly timed for Barcelona's dinner culture. Alternatively, a refined welcome dinner at the hotel's own restaurant to ease into the trip.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light – jet lag and travel fatigue are real. Confirm private transfer in advance. Barcelona restaurants rarely fill before 21:00, so a late dinner reservation is entirely normal and expected.

day_by_day.morning: Sagrada Família Guided Tour – Begin the day with a skip-the-line premium guided tour of Gaudí's iconic basilica. Arrive at opening (09:00) to beat the August crowds and heat. Tower access is included, offering panoramic views over the Eixample grid. A knowledgeable guide will decode the symbolism of the Nativity and Passion facades, the forest-like nave, and the ongoing construction milestones. Allow 2–2.5 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Sagrada Família, take a private car or taxi along Passeig de Gràcia to explore the 'Block of Discord' (Manzana de la Discòrdia) at your own pace – admire Casa Lleó Morera, Casa Amatller, and the jewel of the block, Casa Batlló. Book a premium Casa Batlló 'Magic Nights' or standard daytime ticket in advance. Continue to Casa Milà (La Pedrera) for a rooftop visit during the cooler late afternoon. Grab a cold drink at a terrace café on Passeig de Gràcia.
day_by_day.evening: Palau de la Música Catalana Evening Concert – Dress smartly and attend a live concert inside this breathtaking UNESCO-listed Modernista masterpiece by Lluís Domènech i Montaner. The stained-glass skylight and sculpted stage are extraordinary under evening lighting. Pre-book premium seating well in advance. After the concert, enjoy cocktails at the Palau's own bar or head to El Xampanyet in El Born for cava and pintxos.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel, then a coffee and croissant at a classic Eixample café such as Forn de Sant Jaume near Passeig de Gràcia.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Cervecería Catalana on Carrer de Mallorca – a Barcelona institution for upscale tapas and montaditos. Arrive by 13:30 to secure a table.
meals.dinner: Pre-concert light dinner at Llamber (El Born) – creative Catalan cuisine in an elegant setting, ideal for an early 20:00 reservation before the concert.

day_by_day.notes: August heat peaks between 13:00–17:00 (avg. high ~29°C). Plan outdoor sightseeing in the morning and use air-conditioned venues in the early afternoon. Book Sagrada Família and Palau de la Música tickets months in advance for August.

day_by_day.morning: Gothic Quarter Architecture Walk – Join a small-group premium walking tour through the Barri Gòtic starting at 09:30, when the narrow medieval lanes are still cool and relatively quiet. Discover Roman ruins beneath the city (Temple d'August), the Barcelona Cathedral, Plaça Reial, and hidden courtyards. A specialist architecture guide will contextualise 2,000 years of layered history. The tour typically runs 2–2.5 hours.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the Gothic Quarter, cross into El Born neighbourhood and visit the Museu Picasso (book timed entry in advance) to explore the artist's formative Barcelona years. Afterwards, browse the boutiques of El Born and visit the stunning Santa Maria del Mar basilica – a masterpiece of Catalan Gothic architecture, free to enter. Rest at the hotel during peak heat (14:30–17:00) or enjoy the hotel pool if available.
day_by_day.evening: Tapas Crawl on Carrer del Parlament – Head to the vibrant Sant Antoni neighbourhood for a curated premium tapas crawl. Begin with vermouth at Bar Calders, move to patatas bravas and jamón at Federal Café or Bodega Sepúlveda, and finish with creative pintxos at Morro Fi. The neighbourhood buzzes with a sophisticated local crowd from 20:00 onwards. End the night with cocktails at a rooftop bar such as Paradiso (El Born) – ranked among the world's best bars.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the hotel, then pick up a fresh pastry from a local bakery near the Gothic Quarter before the tour.
meals.lunch: Lunch at El Xampanyet (El Born) – a legendary cava bar serving anchovies, cheese, and cold cuts. Arrive early (13:00) as it fills quickly.
meals.dinner: The tapas crawl on Carrer del Parlament serves as a progressive dinner. Budget €40–60 per person across multiple stops for a premium experience.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes for the Gothic Quarter cobblestones. The Sant Antoni tapas scene is best experienced from 20:00–23:00 when locals are out. Paradiso cocktail bar may have a short queue – worth the wait.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Montjuïc – Take a private car or the Telefèric del Port cable car up to Montjuïc for sweeping harbour views. Visit the Fundació Joan Miró (one of Europe's finest modern art museums) and the Pavelló Mies van der Rohe – the reconstructed 1929 Barcelona Pavilion, a landmark of modernist architecture and a must for architecture enthusiasts. The clean geometry and reflective pools are stunning in morning light. Allow 3 hours across both sites.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the hotel for a midday rest and pool time during peak heat. In the late afternoon (17:00), take a private guided tour of the Recinte Modernista de Sant Pau – Domènech i Montaner's extraordinary hospital complex, a UNESCO World Heritage Site and arguably the most underrated Modernista building in Barcelona. The ornate pavilions and gardens are magnificent and far less crowded than Sagrada Família.
day_by_day.evening: Razzmatazz Club Night – Experience Barcelona's legendary nightlife at Razzmatazz, one of Europe's top clubs featuring five rooms across multiple music genres (electronic, indie, pop, techno). Book a premium table or VIP entry in advance. Barcelona nightlife starts late – pre-drinks at a cocktail bar such as Dry Martini (Eixample) from 22:00, then head to Razzmatazz from midnight. The club runs until 06:00.

meals.breakfast: Full breakfast at the hotel to fuel a busy day.
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the Fundació Joan Miró's terrace café or a nearby restaurant in Montjuïc before returning to the hotel.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Tickets (Albert Adrià's avant-garde tapas restaurant, book months ahead) or Bodega 1900 (same group, more accessible) – both are world-class and perfectly timed for a 21:00 reservation before a late club night.

day_by_day.notes: Razzmatazz is located in Poblenou (~15 min taxi from the hotel area). Pre-book VIP table service for the best experience. Pace yourself – this is a late night. Consider a late checkout or nap before the evening. August rain probability is low but carry a light layer for air-conditioned venues.

day_by_day.morning: After a late night at Razzmatazz, enjoy a leisurely late breakfast at the hotel (until 11:00). Then take a relaxed private car ride to Park Güell for a final Gaudí experience – book a timed entry ticket for the Monumental Zone (the iconic mosaic terrace and Hypostyle Room). The park's architecture and city views are spectacular. Visit by 10:00–11:00 if energy allows, or push to a 12:00 slot for a slower morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final afternoon of luxury shopping along Passeig de Gràcia and the Diagonal – browse flagship stores, local Catalan design boutiques, and pick up premium souvenirs (Escribà chocolates, Colmado Quilez delicacies, or a bottle of aged Priorat wine). Visit the rooftop of La Pedrera one final time at golden hour if not done on Day 2, or simply enjoy a long, indulgent lunch. Return to the hotel to pack and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at a celebrated Barcelona restaurant – Disfrutar (ranked #1 in The World's 50 Best Restaurants 2023, book far in advance) for a once-in-a-lifetime avant-garde tasting menu, or Lasarte (3 Michelin stars) for impeccable Basque-Catalan haute cuisine. End with a nightcap at the rooftop bar of Hotel Arts or W Barcelona for panoramic sea views – a perfect farewell to the city.

meals.breakfast: Late, leisurely breakfast at the hotel – order à la carte and take your time.
meals.lunch: Casual but quality lunch at Bar Mut (Eixample) – a classic Barcelona brasserie with excellent seafood and wine list.
meals.dinner: Farewell tasting menu at Disfrutar or Lasarte. Budget €200–300 per person with wine pairing. Reserve 3–6 months in advance for August.

day_by_day.notes: Check hotel checkout time and arrange luggage storage if your departure flight is later in the day or the following morning. Confirm private transfer back to El Prat Airport. Tip generously at restaurants and with your driver – service culture in Barcelona appreciates it. Keep a light rain jacket accessible as August can occasionally bring brief afternoon thunderstorms (47.5mm monthly average).

query: Barcelona architecture and nightlife, $2000, 5 days, August from NYC
